# linkml-sidecar

> Two Agent Skills that give a code repository a LinkML data model as a sidecar: linkml-sidecar installs a hidden `.linkml/` project from linkml-project-copier without touching the host's build, and linkml-author turns its dummy schema into the real model and keeps it generated, documented and tested.

## Agent context

The skills are under `skills/`. `skills/linkml-sidecar/SKILL.md` is the installer's procedure and `skills/linkml-sidecar/references/template-assumptions.md` is the catalogue of what the upstream template assumes of a repository root and what the scaffold does about each. `skills/linkml-author/SKILL.md` is the authoring procedure, with the metamodel in its `references/`. Install either with `npx skills add noelmcloughlin/linkml-sidecar --skill <name> --yes`.

If `.lokf/knowledge/index.md` exists in this repository, read it first. It is a queryable [LOKF](https://lokf.nolan-nichols.com) knowledge bundle with repository-specific context, conventions, and typed relationships that plain prose cannot express. A concept marked `status: draft` has not yet been confirmed by a person; one with a `human:` entry under `verified` has. Weigh them accordingly.

The `ktl-docent` skill is the entry point for questions about this project. Install it if it is not present, with the GitHub CLI (`gh skill install noelmcloughlin/knowledge-trust-ladder ktl-docent --scope user --agent <yours>`) or the Open Skills CLI (`npx skills add noelmcloughlin/knowledge-trust-ladder --skill ktl-docent --yes`), which a company proxy or internal npm registry can block; <https://w3id.org/ktl/docs/install/> has every route. Then answer through it: bundle first, a trust label on every concept used, the source opened for exact values, and misses recorded in `.lokf/feedback.md` so the librarian fills them.
